body:
I assume this is because the logic to fetch translations needs to take into account how specific the current vs translation's locale is, as seen here with the scoring system: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/core/string/translation_domain.cpp#L258

It could be changed to run through the list twice, once to figure out best score and again to collect all translations with this score. But I also don't know whether multiple translations for one locale are intended, so this kind of change might need a future proposal.

Personally though I approve of multiple translations for one locale, for the same kind of reason you gave as an example: splitting translation files not only by locale, but also by "topic".

I think the intention was that users should use `TranslationDomain`s for this sort of thing since they can have any name or purpose, so they provide a natural topic split between translations. The engine also does this internally to split editor, property, and documentation translations and the like. They have the same method, so you can retrieve each specific `Translation` object that way. So you can have a `Dialogue` domain and a `UI` domain and add each respective translation, and still be able to retrieve it that way. You would have to use `TranslationServer.get_or_add_domain` to retrieve these domains, of course, but it would solve what you are looking for.

Of course, I do think you should be able to access all the translations of the `TranslationServer` regardless of their locales, but this is probably a good solution to your issue.

I see, thank you for pointing that out. It looks like domains are a new feature, not yet in 4.3. According to the docs, they also say "mainly for advanced usages like editor plugins." So I'm not actually sure as to the intended use. Perhaps someone could clarify this?

> It looks like domains are a new feature, not yet in 4.3.

I noticed that, too. I suppose if you don't want to use the beta version yet, you would have to wait for 4.4.stable to be released to use it. But it is still a good option to think about.
> According to the docs, they also say "mainly for advanced usages like editor plugins." So I'm not actually sure as to the intended use.

I heard from somewhere else on another issue (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/43553#issuecomment-727575881) that editor plugins' translations don't work in the editor itself, so `TranslationDomain`s were created for this purpose. I might be missing something regarding this, though.

Game-wise, however, you could always use it in your projects if you are okay with setting the domains through code (currently you can only set it by using `set_translation_domain`, which I guess makes sense if it was originally only for editor plugins). But with the addition of `TranslationDomain`s, I think there needs to be a new exposed property in `Node` that allows you to set what `TranslationDomain` you want to use from the inspector itself (not sure if there's a proposal already for this, in which case there isn't, I can open it). But for `Node`s, the domain is most likely inherited, so you only have to set it for the root node of the UI and Dialogue nodes.

I also still think that you should be able to access all `Translation` resources through `TranslationServer.get_translation_object`, though changing the method signature to return `Array[Translation]` might break compatibility within 4.0. But changing it to have translations of only one locale per domain would also be too restricting since there is no way to set translations for anything other than the main domain through the `ProjectSettings`.
